title: Upper zone sensor fault
shortDescription: Upper compartment thermistor open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Maytag dual-zone wine coolers display E1 when the upper compartment temperature sensor reading is invalid. Without a working sensor, temperature regulation is not possible.

Replace the thermistor or repair the wiring harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power, locate sensor, splice replacement.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is sealed in the foam.

faq.a: Possibly, transfer to working storage if temperatures drift.

title: Lower zone sensor fault
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the lower zone thermistor is open, shorted, or unplugged. Cooling for that zone is suspended.

Replace the sensor or fix the harness routing.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Access from rear panel and replace thermistor.

faq.q: Can both zones fail at once?
faq.a: Yes, if a connector at the board is loose.

title: Door open alarm
shortDescription: Door has been open for over 5 minutes.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates the door switch reports the door open beyond the alarm timeout. Make sure bottles are not blocking the door, and verify the door switch and gasket.

Replace the magnetic switch if needed.
whenToCallPro: If switch is integrated with hinge.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag wine cooler E3 door open

faq.a: Cooling continues but compressor cycles excessively.

title: Defrost system fault
fullDescription:
E4 indicates frost buildup on the evaporator coil could not be cleared in the expected time. Causes include a failed defrost heater, a stuck damper, or a failed thermostat.

Manual defrost (24 hour power-off) often clears the immediate fault.
whenToCallPro: For heater replacement inside the cabinet.

title: Compressor fault
fullDescription:
E5 is shown when the compressor relay activates but no current flow is detected, or the overload trips repeatedly. The fault may be a relay, run capacitor, or a seized compressor.

Professional service is recommended for sealed system work.

faq.a: Often more cost-effective than compressor swap.

title: Fan fault
shortDescription: Evaporator or condenser fan not spinning.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates the controller is not seeing the expected fan tach signal. The fan may be obstructed, the bearing seized, or the motor failed.

Clear obstructions, then test for power at the motor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fans
fixSteps.instruction: Pull rear panel, manually rotate fans.

whenToCallPro: If fan is in foam-sealed area.

faq.a: Yes, evap and condenser are independent.

title: High temperature alarm
fullDescription:
HI alarm is set when interior temperature stays above the warning level for over 2 hours. Often follows door-left-open events, but can indicate cooling system failure.

Verify door seal and condenser cleanliness.
whenToCallPro: If HI persists clean and closed.

faq.a: Brief warm exposure usually does not damage wine.

title: Low temperature alarm
fullDescription:
LO indicates the temperature dropped below 38F for an extended period. A stuck damper or failed thermostat is likely.

Wines may freeze; remove bottles immediately.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag wine cooler LO too cold

faq.a: Pop corks before freeze cracks them.

title: Power failure recovery
fullDescription:
PF flashes after the unit detects a mains power interruption. Press any button to acknowledge.

No action needed beyond verifying setpoints.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag wine cooler PF power fail

title: Communication fault
shortDescription: Display board lost contact with main board.
fullDescription:
CF indicates loss of communication between the user interface and main control. Typically a loose ribbon or moisture issue.

Reseat connectors after powering down.

faq.a: Yes, main board still controls compressor.
